findings.claim: `linearIndepOn_root_baseOf` is specialized to `ℚ`, but the preceding lemma `linearIndepOn_root_baseOf'` was set up precisely to allow an arbitrary ordered coefficient ring `S` with `[P.IsValuedIn S]`. This loses generality in the exported API and forces downstream users back to `ℚ` even when they already work over another ordered coefficient system.
findings.suggested_fix: Generalize the final theorem to the same `S`-parameter setup as `linearIndepOn_root_baseOf'` (or add such a generalized theorem alongside the `ℚ` specialization). Concretely, mirror the assumptions `[LinearOrder S] [CommRing S] [IsStrictOrderedRing S] [Algebra S R] [FaithfulSMul S R] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower S R M] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower S R N] [P.IsValuedIn S]` and conclude `LinearIndepOn R P.root (baseOf P.root (f : M →+ S))`.

findings.claim: The new `self_*` lemmas duplicate an established naming pattern already present in this interval API: `notMem_Ioi_self`/`notMem_Iio_self` exist in the same file, while the renamed membership lemmas become `self_mem_Ici`/`self_mem_Iic`. Introducing `self_notMem_Ioi` and `self_notMem_Iio` gives two competing names for the same facts in one file, which is an API inconsistency rather than a pure refactor.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the `self_mem_Ici` / `self_mem_Iic` rename, but do not add `self_notMem_Ioi` / `self_notMem_Iio`. Instead deprecate the old `x ∈ Ixx ↔ False` lemmas to the existing declarations `notMem_Ioi_self` and `notMem_Iio_self` (or, if you want symmetry, rename those existing declarations rather than adding duplicates).
findings.evidence: target/Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/Basic.lean already contains `theorem notMem_Ioi_self : a ∉ Ioi a` and `theorem notMem_Iio_self : b ∉ Iio b`, while this PR adds `theorem self_notMem_Ioi : a ∉ Ioi a` and `theorem self_notMem_Iio : a ∉ Iio a`.

findings.claim: `dist_le_dist_of_mapsTo_ball_self` no longer proves the advertised/self version: the theorem name and docstring say a fixed-center statement `dist (f z) c ≤ dist z c`, but the new statement only concludes `dist (f z) (f c) ≤ dist z c` and has dropped the `f c = c` hypothesis. This is an API break and also makes `norm_le_norm_of_mapsTo_ball_self` rely on a theorem whose name/doc no longer match its actual content.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the old API by restoring the hypothesis `hc : f c = c` and the conclusion `dist (f z) c ≤ dist z c`, proving it via `dist_le_div_mul_dist_of_mapsTo_ball hd (by rwa [hc]) hz`, or rename/re-document the new theorem to something like `dist_le_dist_of_mapsTo_closedBall_center_image` and add a compatibility theorem with the old name for the fixed-point specialization.

findings.claim: The two new public lemmas are undocumented, while the surrounding API in this section gives docstrings for each translation-invariance lemma. In this part of Mathlib we generally document exported lemmas, especially when adding symmetric variants to an existing API.
findings.suggested_fix: Add docstrings parallel to the existing ones, e.g. `/-- The iterated derivative commutes with shifting the function by a constant to the right using subtraction. -/` before `iteratedDeriv_comp_sub_const` and `/-- The iterated derivative of `fun z ↦ f (s - z)` picks up a factor `(-1)^n`. -/` before `iteratedDeriv_comp_const_sub`.

findings.claim: The new `n = 0` branch proves `closure ((1 : Set G)) = ⊥` just to recover `x = 1`. This is correct, but it is an unnecessarily indirect proof for a routine base case and makes the argument harder to read than the old statement it replaces.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the `0` case directly through `pow_zero`: after `simp only [pow_zero] at hx`, derive `hx : x = 1` via a short lemma or an explicit `have hcl : closure ((1 : Set G)) = (⊥ : Subgroup G) := by simpa using (Subgroup.closure_eq_bot_iff.mpr (by rfl))`, then conclude with `simpa [hx]`. If possible, factor out a tiny reusable lemma for `closure ({1}) = ⊥`/membership in it.

findings.claim: The new lemma should be marked `[grind =]` like the surrounding cardinality identities. As written it is not available to `grind` as a rewriting fact, even though the main motivation of the PR is to expose this equality form in addition to the inequality.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the attribute `@[grind =]` to `eq_card_diff_of_sdiff` so automation can use it directly, matching `card_sdiff_of_subset` and `card_sdiff` nearby.

findings.claim: `Groupoid.invEquivalence` is introduced without the corresponding `IsEquivalence` instance for `Groupoid.invFunctor` (or equivalently for `(Groupoid.invEquivalence C).functor`). In nearby CategoryTheory APIs, equivalence constructors usually also expose this instance so existing code can use the functor via typeclass search, not only by naming the equivalence explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an instance after the definition, e.g. `instance : (Groupoid.invFunctor C).IsEquivalence := (Groupoid.invEquivalence C).isEquivalence_functor` (or the equivalent formulation for the new functor field). This matches patterns such as `Opposites.opOpEquivalence`/`(opOp C).IsEquivalence` in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Opposites.lean:144-151`.
findings.evidence: `CategoryTheory.Opposites.opOpEquivalence` is immediately followed by `instance : (opOp C).IsEquivalence := (opOpEquivalence C).isEquivalence_inverse`, and analogous equivalences like `Square.opEquivalence` and `MonoidalOpposite.mopEquiv` package both functor and inverse explicitly.
